# Introduction

Introduce the topic of psychological symptom dynamics, explain why individual differences matter, and briefly describe the purpose of the project.

# Research Question and Hypotheses

State the main research question and the expected relationships between group-level and individual-level symptom networks.

# Workflow

Describe the overall workflow of the project, from generating simulated data to estimating and comparing symptom networks.

## Setup

Load the required R packages and supporting scripts, and configure the project environment.

## Simulate Data

Generate longitudinal data containing daily ratings of six psychological symptoms for multiple simulated participants. Explain the main simulation parameters and assumptions.

## Statistical Analysis

Fit the Bayesian multilevel VAR model to estimate group-level symptom dynamics and fit an individual-level model for Participant 1.

# Results

Present the outputs obtained from the statistical analyses, including estimated temporal relationships and uncertainty.

## Descriptive Statistics

Summarise the simulated dataset, including the number of participants, observations per participant, and distributions of symptom ratings.

## Group-Level and Individual-Level Networks

Visualise and describe the estimated group-level network and Participant 1's individual-level network.

## Comparison of Selected Edges

Compare selected temporal relationships between the group and the individual, highlighting similarities, differences, and uncertainty in the estimates.

# Shiny App

Explain how to launch and use the app, including how to generate example participant data or upload a CSV file and compare symptom networks.

# Discussion

Interpret the results in relation to the research question and explain what the project demonstrates about individual differences in symptom dynamics.
